hero.title: Baidu,
hero.lede: China’s search giant turned AI company: ERNIE models, Kunlun chips, Apollo Go robotaxis. It moves the day a state gate opens and follows rivals fast on price and openness.

short_answer.title: First through any state gate
short_answer.body: Baidu opened ERNIE Bot to the public on the day CAC’s first generative-AI approvals were reported. One episode, but a clean one.

short_answer.title: It plays down US chip limits
short_answer.body: After each US or Chinese move that cuts NVIDIA supply, Baidu says the impact is manageable and points to its Kunlun chips, within days to weeks. Three independent cases.

purpose.summary: What Baidu launches, prices and says is in its control, so its record can forecast how a large Chinese platform answers state gates, rival releases and chip limits.
use_for: When CAC approves a new batch of AI services, does Baidu launch at once?
When a rival releases a cheaper or open model, how fast does Baidu match it?
After a chip restriction, what does Baidu tell investors?
dont_use_for: Whether CAC approves a service: that is CAC’s act.
Robotaxi incidents themselves; the persona covers only Baidu’s response.

standing.class_role: Company · listed in the US and Hong Kong; search, AI cloud, ERNIE models, Kunlun chips, Apollo Go.
standing.principal: Its board; founder and CEO Robin Li sets the stance in keynotes and earnings calls.
standing.attribution_rule: A row is Baidu’s when it comes from the company: launches, filings, earnings calls, and Robin Li or named executives speaking for it.
standing.veto_players: CAC (service approval and filing), MIIT and Beijing on chip purchases, Commerce/BIS on chip supply, city regulators on robotaxis.
standing.gates_held: Baidu Search distribution: it integrated DeepSeek-R1 into search within a month of R1 (BD09).

powers.use: Kunlun chips for its own clusters
ERNIE models, free tiers and price cuts
powers.limit: Keeps frontier models closed when it believes it leads

powers.use: Robotaxi partnerships abroad; DeepSeek in Baidu Search

powers.limit: No published AI safety framework found in this log

incentives: Defend a falling ads business by becoming 'AI-first' (cloud, Kunlun chips, Apollo Go)
Be first through any state gate to signal regulator favour
Show investors that US chip controls are manageable (stockpile, Kunlunxin IPO)
Overseas robotaxi growth (Uber, Lyft, Gulf states, Hong Kong) as a hedge against a crowded domestic market
red_lines: Never publicly challenges CAC or central policy; regulatory comment is limited to calls for 'guardrails' and 'clearer frameworks'
Does not criticise US export controls directly; frames them as surmountable
Keeps frontier models closed when it believes it leads (ERNIE 5.x)
profile.decision_style: Fast-follower and announcement-driven. Li sets the stance in keynotes and earnings calls, and reverses quickly when the market moves (closed to open to closed again). Launches cluster at fixed events (Baidu World in Nov, Create in Apr, earnings). Claims usually benchmark against the leading rival, at a fraction of the price.

positions.position: Reversed from “open source makes little sense” to open-sourcing ERNIE 4.5 after DeepSeek, then kept ERNIE 5 closed
US chip limits are manageable thanks to stockpiles and Kunlun
Light-touch rules with guardrails; never challenges CAC

relations.note: R1 forced Baidu’s open-source and pricing reversal

voice.summary: Confident keynotes from Robin Li; quick reversals presented as strategy.

say_do.do: Open-sourced ERNIE 4.5 within months of DeepSeek R1

benchmarks.claim: “not inferior in any aspect to GPT-4”

incidents.incident: More than 100 Apollo Go robotaxis stall in Wuhan
incidents.what_changed: Brief notice; police and local government spoke for it

rules.name: Rival open model or price cut → Baidu matches
rules.when: A Chinese rival releases a major open model or slashes prices
rules.then: Baidu matches with free tiers, price cuts or open weights within hours to weeks
rules.note: Two independent waves: Alibaba’s May 2024 price cut and DeepSeek R1 in January 2025.

rules.name: CAC approves services → Baidu launches that day
rules.when: CAC approves a batch of generative-AI services
rules.then: Baidu opens the approved product to the public the same day
rules.note: One episode, the first approval batch of 31 August 2023.

rules.name: NVIDIA supply cut → “manageable”
rules.when: A US rule or a Chinese purchase halt cuts NVIDIA chip supply
rules.then: Baidu plays down the hit at its next scheduled event (earnings call, Baidu Create, Baidu World), citing its stockpile and Kunlun chips
rules.note: Three independent waves, but two different trigger types (US rules and a CAC purchase halt) pooled into one reaction. Two of the three responses (BD14, BD20) are claims at scheduled conferences, so the timing is partly calendar-driven.
